text:
Timo Meier just became Switzerland's all-time leading NHL goal scorer, as Daily Faceoff and others noted this week, and he did it in the middle of his best stretch of the season. Seven goals and ten points in his last ten games, five goals in six, with his ice time up about a minute and a half a night after Sheldon Keefe reshuffled the lines. The Meier, Jack Hughes and Connor Brown trio has been the one reporters keep pointing at.

The hot run is earned. Over those ten games his own chances are worth 5.7 expected goals against a usual 4.1, and nobody on the Devils piles up shots like him: 98 in 26 games. The surprising part is that the season total still undersells him. Eight goals on 11.0 expected means he has been unlucky overall, shooting 8.2% against a talent range near 10.5%, and his linemates have finished below their chances too.

New Jersey owns 59% of the expected goals at five on five with him on. If the finishing just evens out, there are more goals in this.
